query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: In an initially single‐phase high-entropy alloy, brittle behavior emerges when the nano‐scale precipitates (e.g., Mn₂O₃) present at cell or incipient grain boundaries coarsen or change in distribution under service conditions, causing them to transition from beneficial Orowan-strengthening agents to stress concentrators that inhibit dislocation motion and dynamic recrystallization.
generation.material_initial_state: An equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy produced by selective laser melting, featuring a single-phase microstructure with a high dislocation density and a fine dispersion of nano-scale Mn₂O₃ precipitates.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled thermal aging treatment within the alloy’s service temperature range to promote modest precipitate coarsening without inducing conventional grain-boundary segregation.
generation.conditions: Mechanical loading at moderate strain rates (≈1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹) and service temperatures between room temperature and approximately 700 °C, where the alloy normally exhibits strong strength–ductility behavior.
generation.structural_mediator: The nano-scale Mn₂O₃ precipitates at cell boundaries and incipient grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Initially, the fine precipitates provide Orowan strengthening and hinder dislocation motion beneficially. Under thermal aging, these precipitates coarsen, increasing local stress concentrations and impeding cooperative slip and dynamic recrystallization, which leads to embrittlement. This contrasts with conventional alloys where toughness degradation is primarily due to grain-boundary segregation and brittle intermetallic formation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Samples subjected to thermal aging that induces precipitate coarsening will show reduced toughness and ductility compared to untreated samples, even while retaining a compositionally complex single-phase microstructure, thereby distinguishing the mechanism from conventional alloy embrittlement.
generation.baseline: The initial SLM-produced HEA state with a fine, uniformly dispersed nano precipitate distribution and high dislocation density, exhibiting combined high strength and ductility under service conditions.
generation.boundary: This mechanistic transition is expected in service conditions up to about 700 °C and under moderate strain rates. The hypothesis may not hold at very low temperatures or under extreme deformation rates where different mechanisms dominate.
generation.uncertainty: The precise thermal aging conditions (temperature and duration) needed to trigger the precipitate coarsening to a critical size that leads to brittle behavior are uncertain. Additionally, how the microstructural evolution quantitatively correlates with toughness loss requires further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA samples manufactured by SLM. Subject one set to a controlled thermal aging treatment (with variations in time/temperature to promote precipitate coarsening) while keeping another set as a baseline (no aging). Conduct uniaxial tensile tests at service-relevant temperatures (e.g., 600–700 °C) and measure toughness and ductility. Follow up with detailed microstructural analysis (using TEM/SEM) to quantify precipitate size and distribution.
measurements: Tensile tests to measure ultimate tensile strength, ductility, and toughness (e.g., fracture energy)
Microstructural characterization (TEM/SEM) to assess precipitate size and distribution changes
Comparative hardness and dislocation density measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal aging treatment does not lead to a measurable decrease in toughness and ductility (i.e., if the aged samples perform similarly to the baseline samples) and there is no corresponding increase in the coarsening of Mn₂O₃ precipitates, then the hypothesis that precipitate coarsening is responsible for brittle behavior in the HEA would be falsified.

System: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Selective laser melting (SLM) using pre-alloyed spherical powder (average diameter 27.2 µm); laser power 90 W, scan speed 600 mm/s, hatch space 80 µm, layer thickness 25 µm, volumetric energy density 75 J/mm³, 180° rotation scanning pattern, high-purity Ar atmosphere.. Test conditions: Compression tests at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C; initial strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; engineering strain limit 0.4; specimens preheated at 10 °C/min; MoS₂ lubricant used..
